metadata.critical_principle: Cross-compilation requires solving the libc selection problem: target binaries link against TARGET libc while build tools run on HOST libc

pkgsCross_architecture.libc_handling: Target binaries link against target libc; build tools use host libc via pkgsCross.<target>.buildPackages
toolchain_components: glibc - Target C library (for dynamic linking)
buildPackages - Host packages needed during build (cmake, python, etc.)

musl_toolchains.purpose: Fully static binaries without dynamic linker dependencies
musl_toolchains.advantage: Single binary runs on any Linux system with compatible kernel
musl_toolchains.limitation: Some packages fail to build with musl (glibc-specific assumptions)

bootstrap_process.stage0: Pre-built cross-binutils from trusted source (SHA-256 verified)
bootstrap_process.stage1: Cross-GCC built using stage0 binutils + host GCC
bootstrap_process.stage3: Production cross-toolchain built using stage2 components
bootstrap_process.verification: Hydra builds stage1 on multiple machines; output hashes must match bit-for-bit (91% reproducibility rate)
bootstrap_process.trust_model: Stage0 binaries trusted; stage1+ verified via reproducibility checks

cmake_pattern.toolchain_file: Can generate CMake toolchain file via pkgs.pkgsCross.aarch64-multiplatform.stdenv.cmake

rust.std_libraries: rust-bin includes pre-built std libraries for common targets (aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu)
rust.proc_macro_challenge: Build scripts (build.rs) and proc-macros compile for HOST but generate code for TARGET
rust.solution: Use cargo-cpuid or conditional compilation to handle architecture-specific code generation

go.native_support: Go has excellent cross-compilation via GOOS/GOARCH
go.cgo_limitation: CGO cross-compilation requires cross toolchain: CGO_ENABLED=1 CC=pkgs.pkgsCross.aarch64-multiplatform.stdenv.cc
go.pure_go: CGO_ENABLED=0 produces fully static binaries without cross toolchain

python.status: Limited support - Python bytecode portable but native extensions require cross toolchain
python.challenge: setup.py often makes host-platform assumptions (e.g., uname detection)
python.solution: Patch setup.py or use environment variables to force target platform

javascript.status: Pure JS portable; native addons (node-gyp) require cross toolchain
javascript.pattern: nodePackages.buildNodePackage with pkgsCross for native addons
javascript.pure_js: No cross-compilation needed - same JS runs on all platforms

qemu_user_mode.purpose: Execute ARM64 binary on x86_64 host
limitations: Cannot test kernel interactions or hardware-specific behavior
Signal handling differences may cause subtle bugs
qemu_user_mode.libc_requirement: Must provide target libc via -L flag (from pkgsCross toolchain)

qemu_system_mode.purpose: Full system emulation for integration testing
qemu_system_mode.workflow: Build NixOS image for target → boot in QEMU → run integration tests
qemu_system_mode.performance: Very slow (10-100x slowdown) but tests full system behavior

remote_hardware.purpose: Deploy to physical ARM/RISC-V hardware for final validation
remote_hardware.automation: Hydra or custom CI can push builds to test farm

cross_compilation_pitfalls: FFI boundaries: Native extensions assume host platform during configuration
Build scripts with uname detection: Must patch or override via environment variables
Filesystem case sensitivity: ARM/RISC-V often use case-sensitive FS; x86 dev machines may not
Endianness issues: RISC-V can be little or big endian; most toolchains assume little-endian
Atomic operation assumptions: ARM32 requires explicit memory barriers for atomics
Unaligned memory access: ARM/RISC-V may fault on unaligned accesses that x86 tolerates
Toolchain path assumptions: Hardcoded /usr/bin/gcc breaks in cross environment

iso_minimal.contents: Minimal NixOS with installer script, no desktop environment

raw_disk_image.purpose: Pre-installed disk image for VMs or SD cards
format_options: raw - Raw disk image (dd-able to SD card)
ext4 - Just filesystem without partition table
raw_disk_image.sd_card_workflow: nix build .#disk-image && sudo dd if=result/sd-image.img of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress

netboot.purpose: PXE boot images for diskless workstations
components: initrd - Minimal initramfs with network drivers

kernel_variants.linux_latest: Latest stable kernel (6.12 as of NixOS 25.11)

initrd_customization.purpose: Early userspace for mounting root filesystem
initrd_customization.contents: Essential drivers, cryptsetup, network tools for netboot

secure_boot.key_management: Requires manual key enrollment in UEFI firmware

device_trees.purpose: Hardware description for ARM systems (replaces PCI enumeration)

limitations: No binary cache - all packages must be built from source
Some packages fail to build due to RISC-V specific issues

pattern.system_detection:
let systems = [ "x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" "riscv64-linux" ];
    forAllSystems = f: builtins.genAttrs systems (system: f nixpkgs.legacyPackages.${system});

hydra_evaluation.purpose: Pre-evaluate flake for all systems to catch cross-compilation errors early
hydra_evaluation.ci_integration: nix flake check --all-systems in CI pipeline

nixos_hardware.benefits: Optimal kernel parameters, firmware, driver configuration for specific devices
